overview: Two DB-backed ticket servers hand out ranges (odd/even) of 10K IDs; app servers allocate locally from their range.
limitations: Range allocation preserves uniqueness, but consumption across servers is not roughly ordered by actual creation time. Prefer Snowflake when the time-order requirement is strict.

estimation.assumption: Range size 10K IDs; illustrative aggregate demand 1M IDs/s.
estimation.result: Most allocations avoid a database round trip; a crash wastes unused IDs.
estimation.implication: Choose ranges to trade fewer DB writes for more gaps, and explicitly relax global creation-time ordering.

components.purpose: User-facing caller for unique id generator.
components.rationale: Keep validation and durable state in services; retry only according to the API contract.

components.purpose: Distribute incoming connections across healthy instances for unique id generator.
components.rationale: Health checks and routing policy support scale-out; connection-based systems need compatible session routing.
Keep request handlers stateless where possible; the datastore or a fenced owner enforces concurrency invariants.

components.purpose: Two ticket servers allocate disjoint odd/even counter ranges using transactional high-water marks. Worker IDs are implicit in the disjoint namespace. Range allocation is monotonic, but local consumption is not timestamp ordered; clock skew does not affect uniqueness.
components.rationale: Document bit width, time ordering, clock behavior, sequence limits and namespace reuse.

components.purpose: Allocate disjoint ranges atomically; lost ranges create gaps and must never be reused.
components.rationale: Choose keys and indexes from the documented access patterns; replicas provide availability, not conflict-free arbitrary writes.

entityDetails.purpose: Durable high-water marks for disjoint ID ranges.
accessPatterns: Atomically reserve a new range; allocate locally until exhausted.
constraints: Never reuse an allocated range; gaps are valid. Global creation-time ordering is not guaranteed.

apiDetails.purpose: Generate a bounded batch of unique IDs.
apiDetails.rationale: Serialize 64-bit integers as strings in JSON. Library mode calls this locally; UUIDv7 returns 128-bit values and requires a relaxed ID-width requirement.

steps.title: Independent range allocators → Ticket high-water marks
steps.explanation: Transactionally advance a high-water mark in a disjoint odd/even namespace. Lost ranges are never reused.

steps.title: Callers → LB → Order Service → Independent range allocators
steps.explanation: Allocate local counters with no DB round trip per ID. IDs are 64-bit but are not globally ordered by actual creation time.

failureCases.scenario: Clock moves backward or a worker lease is reassigned
failureCases.handling: A Snowflake generator stops/waits rather than emitting overlapping timestamps; fence obsolete leases and delay namespace reuse. Ticket ranges avoid clock dependence but lose global time order.

alternatives: Use Snowflake for strict 64-bit roughly time-ordered IDs with disciplined leases and clocks. Use ticket ranges if creation-time order can be relaxed. Use UUIDv7 only if 128-bit width and probabilistic uniqueness are acceptable.
